title: Maiorana–McFarland sign function
statement: For a nonnegative integer $n$, let $\pi$ be a permutation of the binary cube of dimension $n$, and let $g$ assign a sign in $\{-1,1\}$ to each point of that cube. The resulting function on the binary cube of dimension $2n$ sends a point, written as a pair $(x,y)$ of binary $n$-tuples, to $(-1)^{x\cdot\pi(y)}g(y)$, where the dot product is computed in $\mathbb F_2$ and its value is interpreted as an integer sign.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a permutation of the binary cube of dimension $n$
$g$ maps the binary cube of dimension $n$ to $\{-1,1\}$
